**To Reproduce**
1. Send a message to Hermes via WhatsApp
2. Observe that Hermes receives and responds to the message
3. Notice that the WhatsApp sender does NOT see blue tick read receipt indicators

**Expected behavior**
When Hermes reads a WhatsApp message, the read receipt should be sent back so the sender sees the message as read (blue ticks).

**Platform**
- Hermes gateway with WhatsApp platform integration
- SendBlue is no longer used (native WhatsApp integration only)

**Additional context**
This appears to be a one-way flow limitation - messages come in but delivery/read confirmations don't flow back out. The WhatsApp Business API should support this via the /messages endpoint with the  parameter or similar.

This affects user experience as senders don't know their messages have been received and read.

items.title: [Feature]: seekdb M0 (m0) as external memory provider plugin

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

**[seekdb M0](https://m0.seekdb.ai)** is hosted cloud memory, PowerMem-based backend, accessed by HTTP API.

**Concrete use cases**

- Run Hermes (CLI or gateway) with **managed** long-term memory: Access Key (`ak_...`) + optional self-hosted `M0_BASE_URL`, no extra Python SDK for the HTTP path.
- Align with **OpenClaw / Claw** workflows that already use m0 ([SKILL](https://m0.seekdb.ai/SKILL.md)): search, capture pipeline, and CRUD over REST.
- Use `prefetch` / `sync_turn` / `on_memory_write` like Supermemory-style HTTP providers, plus explicit tools (`m0_search`, `m0_store`, etc.) for agent-driven memory ops.

**Summary**

- **Activation:** `memory.provider: m0` with `M0_API_KEY` in `$HERMES_HOME/.env`; optional `M0_BASE_URL` (default `https://m0.seekdb.ai`).
- **Config:** `$HERMES_HOME/m0.json` for `auto_recall`, `auto_capture`, `recall_limit`, `api_timeout`, `search_rewrite`, `base_url` (minimal prompts in `hermes memory setup`; same pattern as Mem0/Supermemory docs).
- **HTTP:** Stdlib client to documented endpoints (`/api/memories/search`, `/api/memories/capture`, `POST /api/memories/`, list/get/update/delete, instance status).
- **DX:** `OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS` entries, `hermes doctor` connectivity check when key is set, user + developer docs, mock-heavy tests + opt-in live tests (`M0_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1`).

### Relation to other work

- **[#6002](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/6002) (PowerMem plugin):** PowerMem targets the **Python SDK** and local/self-managed stack (`powermem`, `powermem.json`). seekdb M0 targets the **hosted HTTP product** at m0.seekdb.ai. They are complementary; only one external `memory.provider` can be active at a time.

### Proposed Solution

Ship a built-in memory provider plugin at `plugins/memory/m0/` implementing `MemoryProvider` and `register(ctx)`.

### Alternatives Considered

- Rely on users maintaining a private fork or a thin wrapper script — higher friction and no shared tests/docs.
- Conflate with PowerMem-only integration — wrong abstraction for users who only have an M0 Access Key and no local PowerMem deployment.

### Feature Type

Enhancement (new memory provider)

### Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)

items.title: bug(telegram): on_processing_complete reaction not firing — ✅ never appears after response
items.body:
## Bug Report

**Reporter:** @willy-scr
**Date:** 2026-04-08
**Related PR:** #5975 (feat(gateway): Discord channel controls + Telegram reactions)

## Description

After enabling `TELEGRAM_REACTIONS=true`, the 👀 (eyes) reaction correctly appears on the user's message when processing begins. However, the ✅ (check mark) reaction **never replaces it** after the bot finishes processing and sends the response.

## Environment
- Platform: Telegram gateway (polling mode)
- OS: Linux (Ubuntu, VPS)
- Hermes version: latest main (post #5975 merge)
- Config: `TELEGRAM_REACTIONS=true` in `.env`

## What works
- `on_processing_start` → 👀 reaction appears on user message ✅
- `_set_reaction` API call succeeds (returns True) ✅

## What doesn't work
- `on_processing_complete` → ✅ reaction never appears ❌

## Root Cause Analysis

`on_processing_complete` in `telegram.py` uses:

```python
chat_id = getattr(event.source, "chat_id", None)
message_id = getattr(event, "message_id", None)
if chat_id and message_id:
    await self._set_reaction(chat_id, message_id, "✅" if success else "❌")
```

If `message_id` is `None` (because `MessageEvent.message_id` might not be populated in certain message flow paths), the entire reaction is silently skipped due to the `if chat_id and message_id:` guard.

The `_run_processing_hook` in `base.py` also catches all exceptions silently at warning level, so any failures go unnoticed.

Gateway log shows the hook fires but reaction never changes:
```
INFO [Telegram] reaction 👀 result: True
```
No ✅ log ever appears.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set `TELEGRAM_REACTIONS=true` in `.env`
2. Start gateway with Telegram adapter
3. Send any message to the bot
4. Observe 👀 appears
5. Wait for bot response
6. Observe ✅ **never** replaces 👀

## Expected Behavior
👀 → ✅ after response is sent

## Actual Behavior
👀 stays permanently, never changes to ✅

items.title: [Bug]: Provider-specific headers (e.g. KimiCLI User-Agent) lost after fallback activation
items.body:
## Bug Description

When the primary model fails and Hermes falls back to a provider that requires provider-specific HTTP headers (e.g. kimi-coding requires `User-Agent: KimiCLI/1.x`), the first API call after fallback succeeds, but **all subsequent calls fail with 403**.

This happens because `_try_activate_fallback()` preserves the client object (which has the correct headers baked in) but saves `self._client_kwargs` with only `api_key` and `base_url` — dropping `default_headers`. Every subsequent request rebuilds the client from `_client_kwargs` via `_create_request_openai_client()`, producing a headerless client that gets rejected.

## Reproduction

1. Set `fallback_model: { provider: kimi-coding, model: kimi-k2.5 }` in `config.yaml`
2. Set primary model to a provider that may experience transient failures (e.g. zai/glm-5-turbo with moderate token usage)
3. Trigger a primary model failure (or temporarily use an invalid primary key)
4. Observe fallback activates successfully ("switching to fallback: kimi-k2.5 via kimi-coding")
5. First tool call after fallback may succeed (uses `fb_client` directly)
6. Subsequent calls fail with 403: `"Kimi For Coding is currently only available for Coding Agents such as Kimi CLI..."`

## Root Cause

In `run_agent.py`, `_try_activate_fallback()` (line ~4908):

```python
self.client = fb_client
self._client_kwargs = {
    "api_key": fb_client.api_key,
    "base_url": fb_base_url,
    # ← default_headers from fb_client are dropped here
}
```

`resolve_provider_client()` in `auxiliary_client.py` correctly injects `KimiCLI/1.3` into the returned OpenAI client:

```python
# auxiliary_client.py line 1314
if "api.kimi.com" in base_url.lower():
    headers["User-Agent"] = "KimiCLI/1.3"
client = OpenAI(api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url, default_headers=headers)
```

The initial `self.client = fb_client` uses this headerized client, but every request goes through `_create_request_openai_client()` → `_create_openai_client(self._client_kwargs)` which constructs a bare `OpenAI(api_key=..., base_url=...)` without headers.

This affects any provider that sets `default_headers` on the OpenAI client:
- **kimi-coding** — requires `User-Agent: KimiCLI/1.x` (hard 403 without it)
- **copilot** — requires GitHub Copilot-specific headers

## Fix

Preserve the fallback client's custom headers when saving `_client_kwargs`:

```python
# In _try_activate_fallback(), after self.client = fb_client:
fb_headers = getattr(fb_client, "_custom_headers", None)
if not fb_headers:
    fb_headers = getattr(fb_client, "default_headers", None)
self._client_kwargs = {
    "api_key": fb_client.api_key,
    "base_url": fb_base_url,
    **({"default_headers": dict(fb_headers)} if fb_headers else {}),
}
```

The OpenAI SDK stores `default_headers` passed to the constructor in `client._custom_headers`, so this correctly round-trips the headers through any client rebuild.

## Related

- #5796 / #5797 — Same class of bug (missing KimiCLI User-Agent) but in the **auxiliary client** custom endpoint path, not the fallback path
- #5669 — Fixes kimi-coding credential pool base_url seeding (different bug, same provider)
- #5561 — Original issue for kimi-coding pool seeding

## Summary

Add a LINE Messaging API gateway adapter for Hermes Agent.

## Motivation

LINE has **over 200M monthly active users** across Asia and is the dominant messaging platform in Taiwan, Japan, and Thailand, but Hermes Agent currently does not support it as a gateway platform.

I’m building a LINE bot for a family insurance brokerage business in Taiwan, so this is not just a theoretical integration.
I have a real production use case to validate it end-to-end.


### Proposed Solution

Add a native LINE Messaging API adapter under `gateway/platforms/line.py`, following the existing gateway platform adapter pattern.

The implementation would likely:
- accept LINE webhook events
- verify the `X-Line-Signature` header before processing
- normalize incoming LINE events into Hermes gateway message handling
- use reply tokens for standard replies
- fall back to the Push Message API when a reply token has expired
- support basic access control via `LINE_ALLOWED_USERS`

Likely files involved:
- `gateway/platforms/line.py`
- `gateway/run.py`
- `gateway/config.py`
- `.env.example`
- `tests/test_line_adapter.py`

Potential environment variables:
- `LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET`
- `LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN`
- `LINE_ALLOWED_USERS`

2. Waiting to see if someone else implements it

items.title: Question: should local STT retry on CPU int8 when faster-whisper hits cuBLAS runtime errors?

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary
I originally noticed this while running `hermes update`, but the more relevant point is *why I had a local modification in `tools/transcription_tools.py` in the first place*.

The local change was not arbitrary customization. It was a small workaround for local STT failure when `faster-whisper` tried to use GPU mode and hit a CUDA/cuBLAS runtime error.

This may overlap with #2885. If so, please feel free to close this as a duplicate. I mainly wanted to document the motivation for the local patch.

## Why I modified this source file locally
My local change added a retry path in `_transcribe_local()`:

- first try `WhisperModel(..., device="auto", compute_type="auto")`
- if transcription raises a `RuntimeError` mentioning `cublas` / `libcublas.so`
- log a warning
- rebuild the model with `device="cpu", compute_type="int8"`
- retry transcription on CPU

In other words, the local patch was trying to turn a hard failure into a graceful fallback.

## Why this seemed useful
For some environments, GPU inference is *partially* available from Python package / wheel perspective, but the actual runtime still fails because the expected CUDA system libraries are not available or not discoverable at execution time.

In that situation, local STT currently fails outright even though CPU inference would still be a perfectly acceptable fallback.

## Practical effect of the local patch
With the fallback patch in place:

- local STT still attempts GPU/auto first
- if the runtime is healthy, behavior stays unchanged
- if the runtime fails specifically on cuBLAS-related errors, transcription still succeeds by retrying on CPU int8

## Why I am opening this
The update conflict merely exposed that I had been carrying this local patch.

The actual question is:

Should Hermes handle this class of `faster-whisper` runtime failure more gracefully upstream by retrying on CPU int8, or is there a different intended fix for this case?

## Environment
- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Branch: `main`
- OS: Linux Mint 22.3 / Ubuntu 24.04 base
- Local STT path involved `tools/transcription_tools.py`

Again: if this is already fully covered by #2885, closing this as duplicate is totally fine. The main thing I wanted to correct is that the important issue is not the updater UX — it is the motivation for the local source modification.

items.title: Zsh completion script fails with eval: _arguments called outside completion context

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug

The zsh completion script generated by `hermes completion zsh` fails when loaded via `eval` as the docs recommend:

```bash
# ~/.zshrc (per docs)
eval "$(hermes completion zsh)"
```

Error on shell startup:
```
_arguments:comparguments:327: can only be called from completion function
```

## Root Cause

The generated script calls `_hermes "$@"` at the top level (line 28), which immediately invokes `_arguments`. When eval'd in `.zshrc`, this runs outside a completion context — `_arguments` is only valid inside a function triggered by zsh's completion system.

```zsh
# Current output of `hermes completion zsh`:
_hermes() {
    ...
    _arguments \
        '-p[Profile name]:profile:($profiles)' \
        ...
}

_hermes "$@"    # <-- This line causes the error
```

## Fix

Replace the trailing `_hermes "$@"` with a `compdef` registration, so the function is only called when the user tab-completes `hermes`:

```zsh
_hermes() {
    ...
    _arguments \
        '-p[Profile name]:profile:($profiles)' \
        ...
}

compdef _hermes hermes    # <-- Register lazily instead of calling immediately
```

This is the standard pattern used by `uv`, `kubectl`, `skaffold`, and other tools that support `eval "$(tool completion zsh)"`.

## Workaround

Install the completion as a file instead of using eval:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.oh-my-zsh/completions  # or ~/.zsh/completions
hermes completion zsh > ~/.oh-my-zsh/completions/_hermes
# Then remove the eval line from ~/.zshrc and source ~/.zshrc
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.7.0 (2026.4.3) + 43 commits (latest main as of 2026-04-08)
- macOS 15.4, zsh 5.9, oh-my-zsh

items.title: [Bug]: <thought> tags from Gemma 4 not stripped from response content
items.body:
## Bug Description

When using Gemma 4 models (26B / 31B) via the Gemini API, the model outputs reasoning blocks wrapped in `<thought>...</thought>` tags. These tags are **not stripped** from the final response shown to the user, so the raw thinking process leaks into the chat output.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Gemini API key with a Gemma 4 model (e.g. `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` or `gemma-4-31b-it`)
2. Send any message that triggers reasoning
3. Observe `<thought>...</thought>` blocks appearing in the visible response

## Expected Behavior

Reasoning blocks should be stripped (or separated) just like `<think>`, `<thinking>`, and `<reasoning>` tags are.

## Actual Behavior

`<thought>...</thought>` content is rendered inline in the response.

## Root Cause

`_strip_think_blocks()` in `run_agent.py` handles several tag variants but is missing `<thought>`:

```python
# run_agent.py ~line 1548
content = re.sub(r'<think>.*?</think>', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL)
content = re.sub(r'<thinking>.*?</thinking>', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
content = re.sub(r'<reasoning>.*?</reasoning>', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL)
content = re.sub(r'<REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>.*?</REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL)
# <thought> is missing here
```

## Proposed Fix

Add one line to `_strip_think_blocks()`:

```python
content = re.sub(r'<thought>.*?</thought>', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
```

And include `thought` in the cleanup regex on the last line of the function:

```python
content = re.sub(r'</?(?:think|thinking|reasoning|thought|REASONING_SCRATCHPAD)>\s*', '', content, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
```

## Environment

- Model: Gemma 4 26B / 31B via Gemini API
- Tag format used by Gemma 4: `<thought>...</thought>`

The memory tool works

## Summary

Currently `display.tool_progress` in `config.yaml` is a global setting that applies uniformly across all platforms (CLI, Telegram, Slack, Discord, etc.). The only exception is webhooks, which are hardcoded to `off`.

## Problem

Different platforms have different verbosity needs. For example, a user may want `verbose` mode in Telegram (personal assistant channel) but `off` in Slack (team workspace where tool chatter is noise).

## Proposed Solution

Add a `tool_progress_overrides` map under `display:` that allows per-platform settings:

```yaml
display:
  tool_progress: all          # global default
  tool_progress_overrides:    # per-platform override
    slack: 'off'
    telegram: verbose
    cli: all
```

### Implementation Notes

- The infrastructure for per-platform config keys already exists via `_platform_config_key()` in `gateway/run.py`
- `platform_toolsets` already follows this per-platform pattern in `tools_config.py`
- The change would be minimal — in the `_handle_message` path around line ~6311 of `gateway/run.py`, check for an override before falling back to the global value:

```python
# Current:
_raw_tp = user_config.get("display", {}).get("tool_progress")

# Proposed:
_overrides = user_config.get("display", {}).get("tool_progress_overrides", {})
_raw_tp = _overrides.get(platform_key) or user_config.get("display", {}).get("tool_progress")
```

- The `/verbose` command could optionally accept a platform argument (`/verbose slack`) or continue to cycle the global default.

## Additional Context

The `platform_key` variable is already computed right above the `tool_progress` resolution (line 6294), so it's available at zero cost.

items.title: Process-wide interrupt singleton causes cross-session contamination on multi-client deployments
items.body:
## Summary

`tools/interrupt.py` exposes a single process-wide
`_interrupt_event = threading.Event()` shared by every concurrent
`AIAgent` in the process. When two or more agents run simultaneously
in the same process — for example two `/v1/chat/completions` clients
on the API server, or a gateway runner with multiple active sessions —
one agent's interrupt fans out to every other agent's tool layer and
produces truncated mid-task completions on unrelated requests.

This is a follow-up to the discussion in #4072 with full reproduction
details. The merged PR #3427 ("true interrupt on SSE disconnect") is
what makes this bug reliably reproducible on the API server, though
the root cause has been latent since the singleton was introduced.

## Affected versions

Verified on `main` at `ff6a86cb` (v0.8.0). The singleton exists
verbatim in every release that ships `tools/interrupt.py`.

## Reproduction (conceptual)

1. Run the API server in a process serving more than one client.
2. Client A sends a `/v1/chat/completions` SSE request that triggers a
   long-running tool call (terminal command, web extract, browser
   navigation, docker exec, etc.).
3. While A's tool is in flight, client A's browser tab closes.
4. `gateway/platforms/api_server.py:749` fires
   `agent.interrupt("SSE client disconnected")`.
5. Client B has a concurrent `/v1/chat/completions` request that is
   also mid-tool.
6. Client B's tool returns `[interrupted]` immediately, the LLM in
   agent B receives the truncated tool result, and emits a premature
   "stop" completion mid-task.

The reverse race exists too: any other request whose
`run_conversation()` starts up calls `clear_interrupt()` →
`_set_interrupt(False)`, silently un-interrupting an agent that
another caller had legitimately stopped.

## Why per-agent flags don't help

Each `AIAgent` has its own `self._interrupt_requested`, but it only
guards the LLM API-call polling loop in `_interruptible_api_call`
(`run_agent.py:4378`). The 11 long-running tools that import
`is_interrupted` from `tools.interrupt` all observe the singleton:

- `tools/terminal_tool.py`
- `tools/web_tools.py`
- `tools/vision_tools.py`
- `tools/browser_tool.py`
- `tools/send_message_tool.py`
- `tools/environments/local.py`
- `tools/environments/docker.py`
- `tools/environments/ssh.py`
- `tools/environments/daytona.py`
- `tools/environments/singularity.py`
- `tools/environments/modal_common.py`
- `tools/environments/persistent_shell.py`

So the per-instance isolation breaks at the tool boundary.

## Why no test catches this

Every interrupt test in `tests/tools/test_interrupt.py` and
`tests/run_agent/test_interrupt_propagation.py` instantiates a single
agent (or a parent/child delegate tree). The dominant CLI and
single-chat Telegram usage patterns serialize per session, so the bug
is invisible outside multi-client deployments — and unsurprisingly no
issue has been filed for this exact failure mode before.

## Proposed fix

Make the interrupt event per-`AIAgent` and bind it to a
`contextvars.ContextVar` for the duration of `run_conversation()`. The
public `is_interrupted` / `set_interrupt` API stays unchanged; the 11
tool modules need no edits. A module-level fallback `Event` is kept
for legacy callers that have not bound a per-agent event (CLI single
agent, tests that import `_interrupt_event` directly).

`ThreadPoolExecutor` workers spawned by `_execute_tool_calls_concurrent`
must inherit the binding via `contextvars.copy_context().run(...)`,
since neither `ThreadPoolExecutor.submit` nor
`asyncio.loop.run_in_executor` propagates contextvars automatically.

PR #6XXX implements this with regression tests covering the cross-
contamination scenarios described above.

cc #4072 #3427

items.body:
# Feature Request: Skill Auto-Detection System

## Summary
Implement automatic skill detection and activation based on conversation context triggers, as documented in the existing `skill-auto-detection` skill but not yet functional.

## Current State
- **Skill exists**: `skill-auto-detection` is documented in `hermes-agent/skill-auto-detection/SKILL.md`
- **Not implemented**: No active auto-detection logic in v0.8
- **Config missing**: `config.yaml` has no `auto_detection` section
- **User impact**: Skills must be manually loaded via `/skill` or `skill_view()`

## Proposed Implementation

### 1. Config Schema Addition
```yaml
skills:
  external_dirs: []
  creation_nudge_interval: 15
  auto_detection:
    enabled: true              # Master switch
    mode: suggest              # Options: silent, suggest, disabled
    min_confidence: 0.6        # Threshold for activation
    max_suggestions: 3         # Limit suggestions per turn
    cache_duration: 300        # Seconds to remember choices
```

### 2. Trigger Types to Support
Each skill's SKILL.md frontmatter should support:

```yaml
---
name: pytorch-ml
description: PyTorch ML workflows
triggers:
  keywords:
    - pytorch
    - torchvision
    - lightning
  filenames:
    - "*.pth"
    - "model.py"
    - "train.py"
  imports:
    - torch
    - torchvision
    - pytorch_lightning
  negative_triggers:
    keywords:
      - tensorflow
      - jax
    imports:
      - tensorflow
  priority: high              # critical | high | medium | low
---
```

### 3. Detection Logic
```python
# Pseudo-code for detection
async def detect_relevant_skills(user_input: str, project_files: list) -> list:
    scored_skills = []
    
    for skill in available_skills:
        score = 0
        
        # Keyword matching (TF-IDF or simple substring)
        for keyword in skill.triggers.keywords:
            if keyword in user_input.lower():
                score += 0.3
        
        # File pattern matching
        for pattern in skill.triggers.filenames:
            if any(fnmatch(file, pattern) for file in project_files):
                score += 0.4
        
        # Import detection (from code snippets in context)
        for module in skill.triggers.imports:
            if f"import {module}" in user_input:
                score += 0.5
        
        # Negative triggers reduce score
        if skill.triggers.negative_triggers:
            for neg_keyword in skill.triggers.negative_triggers.keywords:
                if neg_keyword in user_input.lower():
                    score -= 0.5
        
        if score >= config.min_confidence:
            scored_skills.append((skill, score))
    
    return sorted(scored_skills, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
```

items.title: /compress can report a successful compression even when the transcript is unchanged

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
# Bug report draft: `/compress` reports success even when no compaction occurs

Suggested title:
`/compress` can report a successful compression even when the transcript is unchanged

## Summary

The Telegram/manual gateway `/compress` path can return a success banner like:

`🗜️ Compressed: 19 → 19 messages`
`~11,726 → ~11,726 tokens`

…even when no compaction actually happened.

This is a false positive. The underlying compressor can return the original message list unchanged, but the gateway still rewrites the transcript and formats a success banner as if compression succeeded.

## Actual behavior

Running `/compress` in a gateway session can produce identical before/after message counts and token estimates, with no visible summary inserted and no history trimmed.

Example observed output:

`🗜️ Compressed: 19 → 19 messages`
`~11,726 → ~11,726 tokens`

## Expected behavior

One of these should happen:

1. Actual compaction occurs:
   - message and/or token counts decrease, or
   - a summary/handoff message is inserted and older turns are pruned.

2. If compaction is not possible, the command should return an explicit no-op message, e.g.:
   - `Nothing to compress yet.`
   - `No compression performed: only 19 compressible messages; current settings require more history.`

It should not claim success when the transcript is unchanged.

## Root cause

This appears to be a combination of two behaviors:

1. `ContextCompressor.compress()` intentionally returns the input unchanged for small histories.
2. The manual gateway `/compress` handler does not check whether compression actually changed anything before returning the success banner.

### Why this happens

The gateway manual `/compress` path first filters the transcript down to only `user` and `assistant` messages:

- `gateway/run.py` around lines 4996-5000

```python
msgs = [
    {"role": m.get("role"), "content": m.get("content")}
    for m in history
    if m.get("role") in ("user", "assistant") and m.get("content")
]
```

Then it creates a temporary `AIAgent` and calls `_compress_context(...)` with `quiet_mode=True`:

- `gateway/run.py` around lines 5004-5018

```python
tmp_agent = AIAgent(
    ...,
    quiet_mode=True,
    ...,
)
compressed, _ = await loop.run_in_executor(
    None,
    lambda: tmp_agent._compress_context(msgs, "", approx_tokens=approx_tokens)
)
```

The compressor itself has an early return for small histories:

- `agent/context_compressor.py` around lines 578-586

```python
if n_messages <= self.protect_first_n + self.protect_last_n + 1:
    ...
    return messages
```

With the current defaults, that threshold is effectively:

- `protect_first_n = 3`
- `protect_last_n = 20`
- so compression requires `> 24` messages to do any work.

Those defaults come from `run_agent.py`:

- `run_agent.py` around lines 1093-1097 and 1132-1136

```python
compression_protect_last = int(_compression_cfg.get("protect_last_n", 20))
...
self.context_compressor = ContextCompressor(
    ...,
    protect_first_n=3,
    protect_last_n=compression_protect_last,
)
```

So a 19-message user/assistant history is not compressible by design and is returned unchanged.

However, the gateway handler unconditionally formats a success banner afterward:

- `gateway/run.py` around lines 5037-5040

```python
return (
    f"🗜️ Compressed: {original_count} → {new_count} messages\n"
    f"~{approx_tokens:,} → ~{new_tokens:,} tokens"
)
```

There is no guard for:

- `compressed == msgs`
- `new_count == original_count and new_tokens == approx_tokens`
- a no-op reason such as `too_few_messages`

Because `quiet_mode=True`, the internal warning about not being able to compress is also suppressed, so the failure mode is silent.

## Minimal reproduction

This can be reproduced locally without Telegram by calling the same compression path with a 19-message alternating user/assistant history.

Example reproduction logic:

```python
from run_agent import AIAgent
from agent.model_metadata import estimate_messages_tokens_rough

msgs = []
for i in range(19):
    role = 'user' if i % 2 == 0 else 'assistant'
    msgs.append({'role': role, 'content': f'message {i}'})

orig_tokens = estimate_messages_tokens_rough(msgs)
agent = AIAgent(
    model='openai-codex/gpt-5.4',
    quiet_mode=True,
    max_iterations=1,
    enabled_toolsets=['memory'],
    session_id='compress_bug_repro',
)
compressed, _ = agent._compress_context(msgs, '', approx_tokens=orig_tokens)

print(len(msgs), len(compressed), compressed == msgs)
```

Observed result:

- before messages: 19
- after messages: 19
- transcript identical: `True`

In a real gateway `/compress` flow, that unchanged result still gets presented as a successful compression.

## Impact

- Misleading UX: users are told compression succeeded when nothing changed.
- Harder debugging: no-op cases look like silent failures or “fake compression.”
- Confusing telemetry: operators may assume compaction is working because the banner says it is.
- Manual `/compress` is especially misleading because it filters to only user/assistant turns, so visible conversation length may look “long enough” while the compressible count is still below threshold.

## Suggested fix direction

A good fix would be to return structured outcome metadata from compression, not just the output message list.

For example, manual `/compress` should be able to distinguish:

- `compressed`
- `unchanged_too_few_messages`
- `unchanged_boundary_collapse`
- `unchanged_summary_unavailable`

Minimum viable fix:

1. After `_compress_context(...)`, detect whether the transcript materially changed.
2. Only show the `🗜️ Compressed:` banner if the transcript changed.
3. Otherwise return a no-op explanation with the reason and current threshold.

Optional improvement:

- Make the manual `/compress` response explicitly say it is counting only compressible `user`/`assistant` messages, or reconsider whether manual compression should evaluate the full transcript for eligibility.
- Revisit whether the default `compression.protect_last_n: 20` is too conservative for manual messaging sessions. Lowering it to `10` would reduce the minimum compressible size from `>24` messages to `>14` messages (given the hardcoded `protect_first_n=3`).
- Important nuance: lowering `protect_last_n` is only a tuning/workaround. It does not fix the false-success bug by itself; the command still needs explicit no-op detection.

## Not a duplicate of nearby issues

I checked a few adjacent issues before drafting this:

- `#499` — open enhancement about compaction quality and prompt design, not false-success reporting on no-op manual `/compress`
- `#2153` — closed bug about compression failing to trigger after API disconnects, different failure mode
- `#2771` — open bug about silent memory write failures in gateway sessions, similar "not surfaced to user" pattern but unrelated subsystem

## Environment

- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Branch observed: `main`
- Commit observed locally: `ff6a86cb529a372198b4b80d5e022e32a4a3f2cc`
- Hermes version: `Hermes Agent v0.8.0 (2026.4.8)`
- Python: `3.11.14`
- OS: `Linux 6.17.0-14-generic #14-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Jan 9 17:01:16 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux`
- Reproduced on the gateway/manual `/compress` path and in a direct local Python reproduction

## Relevant code locations

- `gateway/run.py` — `_handle_compress_command()`
- `run_agent.py` — `AIAgent` compressor defaults and `_compress_context()`
- `agent/context_compressor.py` — `ContextCompressor.compress()` early no-op return

## Bug Description

PR #1381 changed `/plan` to use workspace-relative `.hermes/plans/...`, but the current implementation still relies on prompt compliance. In Docker, I observed `/plan` save a plan to `/root/.hermes/plans/...` instead of the active workspace `.hermes/plans/...` under the backend cwd.

I believe the issue is that `build_plan_path()` returns a relative path and the CLI injects a runtime note, but nothing enforces that the eventual `write_file` target stays inside the active workspace. If the model writes `~/.hermes/plans/...`, `tools/file_operations.py` expands `~` against `$HOME`, which is `/root` in the container.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes Agent in Docker with the default image setup.
2. Confirm the runtime environment inside the container is:
   - `PWD=/opt/hermes`
   - `HOME=/root`
   - `HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`
3. Start a CLI session and run `/plan audio extraction batch segmentation`.
4. Let Hermes write the generated plan.
5. Inspect the filesystem inside the container.

## Expected Behavior

The plan should always be written under the active workspace/backend cwd, for example `/opt/hermes/.hermes/plans/<timestamp>-....md`, or the write should be rejected/rewritten if it targets outside that workspace-relative path.

## Actual Behavior

The generated plan was written to:

- `/root/.hermes/plans/2026-04-08_1519-audio-extraction-batch-segmentation.md`

The expected workspace-relative directory was not created:

- `/opt/hermes/.hermes/plans/`

## Affected Component

- CLI (interactive chat)
- Skills (skill loading, skill hub, skill guard)
- Tools (file ops path handling)

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

## Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (Docker on WSL2 host)

## Python Version

`Python 3.13.5`

## Hermes Version

`Hermes Agent v0.7.0 (2026.4.3)`

## Relevant Logs / Traceback

```text
PWD=/opt/hermes
HOME=/root
HERMES_HOME=/opt/data
```

```text
total 8
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 5002 Apr  8 15:19 2026-04-08_1519-audio-extraction-batch-segmentation.md
```

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

- `agent/skill_commands.py` `build_plan_path()` returns `.hermes/plans/...`.
- `cli.py` and `gateway/run.py` only instruct the model to save to that relative path via a runtime note.
- `tools/file_operations.py` expands `~`, so a `write_file` call to `~/.hermes/plans/...` succeeds under `$HOME`.
- That means PR #1381 fixed the intended default target path, but the target is not enforced and can still escape to HOME when the model/tool call deviates from the runtime note.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

- Resolve the runtime plan path to an absolute path inside the active workspace/backend cwd before writing, or
- validate `/plan` file writes and reject or relocate anything outside the expected workspace `.hermes/plans/` directory.
- Disallow `~` and similar home-directory escapes when a runtime save path is supplied.

items.body:
## Problem

After updating hermes-agent, the gateway crashes with:

```
TypeError: ToolRegistry.register() got an unexpected keyword argument 'max_result_size_chars'
```

## Root Cause

1. Commit 65e24c94 added `max_result_size_chars` parameter to `ToolRegistry.register()`
2. Python loaded cached `registry.pyc` (old version without the parameter)
3. `terminal_tool.py` calls `registry.register(..., max_result_size_chars=100_000)`
4. Old cached class rejects the new parameter

## Reproduction

1. Run hermes-agent gateway for a while (generates .pyc cache)
2. Update code (git pull)
3. Restart gateway without clearing cache
4. Gateway crashes on tool import

## Fix

Clear Python cache after update:
```bash
find ~/.hermes/hermes-agent -name '*.pyc' -delete
find ~/.hermes/hermes-agent -name '__pycache__' -type d -exec rm -rf {} +
```

## Suggested Solutions

1. **Startup cache cleanup**: Add cache cleanup in `run_agent.py` or `cli.py` startup
2. **Version-stamped cache**: Use `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` or git hash in cache invalidation
3. **Disable bytecode cache**: Set `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` by default
4. **Setup script**: Clear cache in `setup.sh` or post-update hook

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- Python: 3.12.4
- hermes-agent commit: 65e24c94 (or later)
- Affected profile: life (but could affect any)

items.body:
## Problem

When configuring a custom endpoint via `hermes setup` or `/model`, the setup wizard collects URL, API key, model name, and context length — but never asks which API protocol to use. The `api_mode` is left to auto-detection from the URL.

This breaks when:
- A proxy/gateway serves multiple protocols on the same URL (e.g. LiteLLM proxy that can do both OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages)
- The URL does not contain enough hints for auto-detection (e.g. a plain `https://my-llm.internal/v1` that actually speaks Anthropic Messages)
- Users want to force `codex_responses` for an endpoint that would otherwise default to `chat_completions`

Related: #5718 (hardcoded api_mode for openai-codex provider), #3388 (api_mode drift causing routing failures)

## Proposed Solution

Add an `API protocol` prompt to the custom endpoint setup flow. Default behavior: auto-detect (just press Enter to accept). Users who need to override type `?` to see choices:

```
API protocol [chat_completions] (Enter to accept, ? to choose):
```

If `?` is typed:
```
  1. OpenAI Chat Completions (most common)
  2. Anthropic Messages (Claude-native API)
  3. OpenAI Responses (Codex/GPT-5 reasoning)
  4. Auto-detect from URL (default)
Choice [1-4]:
```

The selected `api_mode` is:
- Saved to `model.api_mode` in config.yaml
- Persisted in `custom_providers` entries so it is restored on provider switch
- Applied in `_model_flow_named_custom` when activating a saved custom provider

## Scope

- `_model_flow_custom()` — add api_mode prompt after context length
- `_model_flow_named_custom()` — read and apply saved api_mode
- `_save_custom_provider()` — persist api_mode in custom_providers entries
- New helper `_prompt_api_mode_selection()` — lightweight prompt with Enter-to-accept default

No changes to auto-detection logic itself — this only adds an explicit override path.

items.title: [Bug]: model-switch requests can be reported as complete before the current live session actually changes
items.body:
## Summary
When asked in a Telegram thread to switch to GPT-5.4 high reasoning and make that the default, Hermes can report success too early: it says the change is "all set" even though the current live session is still on the old model when immediately checked.

This is a false-success bug. The assistant may update future default config, but it still frames the user request as complete before verifying whether the active session actually changed.

## Bug type
Behavior bug / model-switch state reporting bug

## Why this is not a duplicate
I checked adjacent model-switch issues first:
- #5999 asks for a `/model` command in active sessions.
- #3263 is about configuration persistence loss and missing pre-fills in the model switcher UI.

Those are related, but this report is narrower: Hermes told the user the switch was complete even though the current Telegram session was still on the previous model.

## Steps to reproduce
1. In a Telegram DM topic, ask Hermes to switch itself to another model now and also make that model the default.
2. Hermes edits config / reports completion.
3. Immediately ask `What model are you?`
4. Observe that Hermes may admit the current live chat is still on the old model.

## Expected behavior
Hermes should clearly distinguish between:
- `future default changed`, and
- `current session changed`.

It should not say the request is fully complete unless the response also verifies the state the user actually asked for.

## Actual behavior
Hermes said:
- `All set. GPT-5.4 high-level thinking is now the default for Hermes.`

Then one message later, when asked `What model are you?`, Hermes said:
- `In this chat right now, I’m still GPT-5 Codex ... My earlier “all set” answer was too loose — this live conversation itself did not hot-swap models.`

## Reproduction
Session `20260408_113631_ade5a420`
- User `9830`: `Okay, you should be using GPT 5.4 high-level thinking, and also that should be the default for all of Hermes.`
- Assistant `9831`: `Got it—I’ll switch over ...`
- Assistant `9839`: `All set. GPT-5.4 high-level thinking is now the default for Hermes.`
- User `9875`: `What model are you?`
- Assistant `9880`: `In this chat right now, I’m still GPT-5 Codex ... My earlier “all set” answer was too loose ...`
- User had to push again (`9957`, `10057`) before Hermes finally restarted and confirmed GPT-5.4/high.

## Impact
- Breaks trust on configuration/runtime changes.
- Makes the user re-check basic state manually because success messages are not reliable.
- Confuses current-session state with future-session defaults.
- Produces extra friction exactly when the user is trying to steer the runtime deliberately.

## Likely cause / hypothesis
Hermes lacks a strong verification/reporting boundary between:
- persisted default config,
- gateway reload/restart state,
- and the model bound to the current live session.

That makes it easy for the assistant to overclaim completion after editing config, even though the live session remains unchanged.

## Suggested fix direction
1. Add a verification rule: model-switch responses must explicitly report both `current session` and `future default` state.
2. If active-session switching is not supported, force the assistant to say that directly instead of saying `all set`.
3. Add regression coverage for `switch now` followed by `What model are you?` in the same Telegram topic.
4. Consider tying this to a first-class gateway model-switch path instead of ad hoc config edits.

## Environment
- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Observed commit: `ff6a86cb529a372198b4b80d5e022e32a4a3f2cc`
- Observed version: `v2026.4.8-1-gff6a86cb`

- OS: `Linux 6.17.0-14-generic x86_64`
- Platform: Telegram DM topics

items.title: [Bug]: `build_context_files_prompt()` raises PermissionError when TERMINAL_CWD points to an inaccessible directory (eg Daytona)
items.body:
### Bug Description


When Hermes runs as a non-root user on the host (e.g. a dedicated `hermesadmin` account on a VPS), which should be the canonical way, with a Daytona sandbox backend, the agent crashes during system prompt construction with:

```
[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/AGENTS.md'
```

The root cause is a boundary violation between the host runtime and the sandbox environment. `TERMINAL_CWD` is set to `/root` (the correct working directory inside the Daytona sandbox), but `build_context_files_prompt()` in `prompt_builder.py` uses this value to search the **host** filesystem for context files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.hermes.md`). Since the host user cannot read `/root`, the `Path.exists()` / `Path.is_file()` calls raise `PermissionError`.

The functions `_load_agents_md`, `_load_claude_md`, `_load_cursorrules`, and `_find_hermes_md` all have `try/except` blocks around `read_text()`, but the filesystem existence checks (`candidate.exists()`, `candidate.is_file()`) are **outside** these handlers, so `PermissionError` propagates uncaught.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install hermes-agent on a Linux host as a non-root user (e.g. `hermesadmin`, uid=1000)
2. Configure a Daytona sandbox backend
3. Run any skill or workflow that triggers agent initialization (e.g. `workflow-save-emails-rss-jobs`)
4. The agent crashes during `build_context_files_prompt()` before any tool execution

### Expected Behavior

Context file discovery should fail gracefully when `TERMINAL_CWD` points to a directory the host user cannot access. The agent should continue initialization and skip context files it cannot read.

### Actual Behavior


```
Error during OpenAI-compatible API call #3: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/AGENTS.md'
```

The agent crashes and the workflow cannot proceed.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Hermes Version

0.7

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell
Error during OpenAI-compatible API call #3: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/AGENTS.md'
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The call chain is:

1. `run_agent.py:2735` reads `TERMINAL_CWD="/root"` (set by `terminal_tool.py:511` as the default for Daytona backends)
2. `run_agent.py:2736` passes it to `build_context_files_prompt(cwd="/root")`
3. `prompt_builder.py:938` resolves `Path("/root")` on the **host** filesystem
4. `prompt_builder.py:944` calls `_load_agents_md(cwd_path)` (and the other loaders)
5. `_load_agents_md` (line 862) calls `candidate.exists()` on `Path("/root/AGENTS.md")`
6. `Path.exists()` raises `PermissionError` because the host user cannot read `/root`

The `try/except Exception` at line 863-870 only wraps `read_text()`, not the `exists()` check.

The same pattern affects `_load_claude_md`, `_load_cursorrules`, and `_find_hermes_md`.

Move the `candidate.exists()` / `candidate.is_file()` calls inside the existing `try/except` blocks so that `PermissionError` (and any other `OSError`) is caught and logged at debug level, matching the existing error-handling intent.

Example for `_load_agents_md`:

```python
def _load_agents_md(cwd_path: Path) -> str:
    for name in ["AGENTS.md", "agents.md"]:
        candidate = cwd_path / name
        try:
            if candidate.exists():
                content = candidate.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
                if content:
                    content = _scan_context_content(content, name)
                    result = f"## {name}\n\n{content}"
                    return _truncate_content(result, "AGENTS.md")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug("Could not read %s: %s", candidate, e)
    return ""
```

items.title: /compress can report higher token counts after successful compaction because the banner uses a rough transcript-only estimate
items.body:
Suggested title:
`/compress` can report higher token counts after successful compaction because the banner uses a rough transcript-only estimate

## Summary

The gateway/manual `/compress` path can successfully compact a session and still report a larger token count afterward.

Observed example:

`🗜️ Compressed: 27 → 13 messages`
`~4,462 → ~4,727 tokens`

The compaction did happen: the message count dropped sharply and the compressed transcript was rewritten. But the token figure increased because the banner is not reporting real request-token pressure. It is reporting a rough estimate of only the surviving `user`/`assistant` transcript content, and the compactor can replace many short turns with one dense handoff summary.

This makes the `/compress` banner misleading even when compression succeeds.

## Actual behavior

A manual `/compress` can produce output where:

- the message count decreases substantially
- the compressed transcript materially changes
- but the reported token estimate increases

Example observed output:

`🗜️ Compressed: 27 → 13 messages`
`~4,462 → ~4,727 tokens`

In the affected session, the compressed transcript's handoff summary accounted for most of the remaining rough token count.

## Expected behavior

The `/compress` response should do one of the following:

1. Report a metric that actually reflects post-compaction request pressure, or
2. Clearly label the current metric as a rough transcript-only estimate, or
3. Warn when the summary became denser even though the session compacted successfully

It should not implicitly suggest that compaction “made things bigger” without explaining that the displayed number is a limited heuristic.

## Root cause

This is caused by a mismatch between what the banner measures and what compression is optimizing.

### 1. The `/compress` banner measures only filtered transcript content

The manual gateway handler filters history down to only `user` and `assistant` messages with content, then computes `approx_tokens` and `new_tokens` with `estimate_messages_tokens_rough()`:

- `gateway/run.py` around lines 4996-5002
- `gateway/run.py` around lines 5034-5039
- `agent/model_metadata.py` around lines 975-978

That estimator is just:

```python
total_chars = sum(len(str(msg)) for msg in messages)
return total_chars // 4
```

So the banner does **not** reflect:

- the full request payload
- tool messages
- system prompt size
- tool schema size
- provider-reported prompt tokens

It is only a rough char-count heuristic over a filtered transcript.

### 2. The compressor can replace many short turns with one dense summary

The context compressor is explicitly allowed to generate large structured handoff summaries:

- `agent/context_compressor.py` around lines 191-200
- `agent/context_compressor.py` around lines 272-285

The summary budget has:

- a floor of 2000 tokens
- a ceiling of 12000 tokens

The compressor also performs iterative summary updates, preserving the previous summary and adding new progress on later compressions.

That means compression can turn many small conversational turns into one information-dense summary containing:

- decisions
- file paths
- commands run
- errors
- next steps
- critical context

### 3. With current defaults, `27 → 13` is a valid compression outcome

Current compression behavior uses:

- `protect_first_n = 3`
- `compression.protect_last_n = 10` in my local config

The compressor can also merge the summary into the first kept tail message when role alternation would otherwise break.

That makes a result like `27 → 13` entirely plausible:

- 3 protected head messages
- 10 protected tail messages
- summary merged into the first kept tail message

So the observed message-count reduction is consistent with successful compaction.

## Minimal reproduction

I reproduced this locally by forcing a dense compaction summary into a 27-message alternating `user`/`assistant` history.

Observed local result:

- before messages: 27
- after messages: 13
- before rough tokens: 1681
- after rough tokens: 4565

In other words: fewer messages, larger rough token estimate.

I also inspected the real compressed session lineage and found that the surviving handoff summary accounted for most of the remaining rough token count in the compressed child session.

## Impact

- Misleading UX: the user sees “Compressed” but the token number goes up
- Operator confusion: it looks like compaction failed or made the context worse
- Harder debugging: the banner mixes a valid compaction result with a misleading metric
- Adjacent to #6202: even when `/compress` is not a no-op, the success banner can still mislead in a different way

## Not a duplicate of nearby issues

I checked these adjacent issues:

- `#6202` — `/compress` can report success even when the transcript is unchanged
  - Different bug: false-positive success on a no-op
  - This new issue is about a **real** compaction whose displayed token estimate still becomes misleading

- `#2599` — GLM gateway sessions can undercount request size and post-compaction reporting can describe transcript-only size instead of full request size
  - Adjacent but different scope
  - #2599 is about overflow protection and full-request estimation in GLM sessions
  - This new issue is about `/compress` UX in normal operation when dense summaries make the transcript-only heuristic increase after successful compaction

- `#499` — compaction quality overhaul
  - Enhancement request, not a bug report about misleading post-compaction metrics

## Suggested fix direction

Minimum viable fix:

1. Change the `/compress` banner text to explicitly label the number as a rough transcript-only estimate.
2. If `new_tokens > approx_tokens` while `new_count < original_count`, include an explanation such as:
   - `Compression succeeded, but the handoff summary is denser than the removed turns, so the rough transcript estimate increased.`

Stronger fix:

3. Report both:
   - transcript-only rough estimate
   - full next-request rough estimate via `estimate_request_tokens_rough()` or equivalent
4. Prefer provider-reported post-compaction prompt usage when available instead of the current transcript-only heuristic.

## Environment

- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Branch observed: `main`
- Commit observed locally: `ff6a86cb529a372198b4b80d5e022e32a4a3f2cc`
- Hermes version: `Hermes Agent v0.8.0 (2026.4.8)`
- Python: `3.11.14`
- OS: `Linux 6.17.0-14-generic #14-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Jan 9 17:01:16 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux`
- Reproduced on the gateway/manual `/compress` path and via direct local reproduction against the compressor logic

## Relevant code locations

- `gateway/run.py` — `_handle_compress_command()`
- `agent/model_metadata.py` — `estimate_messages_tokens_rough()`
- `agent/context_compressor.py` — summary budget, iterative summary updates, and summary merge behavior
- `run_agent.py` — `AIAgent` compressor defaults

## Expected behavior
When `slack.require_mention: false` is set in `config.yaml`, the bot should respond to all messages in subscribed channels (where `message.channels` event is subscribed), even without @mention.

## Actual behavior
The bot only responds to:
- Messages with @mention
- Replies in threads where it was previously mentioned
- Existing thread sessions

Messages without @mention in non-threaded channels are ignored, even with `require_mention: false`.

## Root cause
In `gateway/platforms/slack.py` around line 833, the code reads `require_mention` from `self.config` as a direct attribute, but it's actually stored in `self.config.extra['require_mention']` (see `gateway/config.py` lines 529-543).

## Fix
Change line 834 in `gateway/platforms/slack.py` from:
```python
require_mention = getattr(self.config, 'require_mention', True)
```

To:
```python
require_mention = self.config.extra.get('require_mention', True)
```

## Workaround
Patch `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/gateway/platforms/slack.py` with the fix above, then restart the gateway.

items.title: [Bug]: Fork bomb regex in dangerous command detection is broken — unescaped metacharacters
items.body:
## Bug Description

The fork bomb detection pattern in `tools/approval.py` line 41 uses unescaped regex metacharacters `()` and `{}`, causing the pattern to never match an actual fork bomb. This completely bypasses the dangerous command approval system for fork bombs.

## Steps to Reproduce

```python
import re
pattern = r':()\s*{\s*:\s*\|\s*:&\s*}\s*;:'
print(re.search(pattern, ':(){ :|:& };:'))  # None — no match
```

## Expected Behavior

The pattern should match the bash fork bomb `:(){ :|:& };:` and trigger the dangerous command approval flow.

## Actual Behavior

`re.search()` returns `None` because `()` creates an empty capture group and `{}` is interpreted as a repetition quantifier, so the pattern silently fails to match.

## Affected Component

- Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

## Root Cause Analysis

File: `tools/approval.py`, line 41

```python
(r':()\s*{\s*:\s*\|\s*:&\s*}\s*;:', "fork bomb"),
```

The parentheses and braces need to be escaped with backslashes for literal matching in regex.

## Proposed Fix

```python
(r':\(\)\s*\{\s*:\s*\|\s*:&\s*\}\s*;:', "fork bomb"),
```

Verified:
```python
import re
fixed = r':\(\)\s*\{\s*:\s*\|\s*:&\s*\}\s*;:'
print(re.search(fixed, ':(){ :|:& };:'))  # <re.Match object>
```

items.title: [Bug]: RPC socket created world-accessible in /tmp — local privilege escalation

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

items.body:
## Bug Description

The code execution sandbox creates a Unix domain socket at a predictable path (`/tmp/hermes_rpc_<uuid>.sock`) with default permissions after `socket.bind()`. On shared systems, any local user can connect to this socket and execute tool calls (terminal commands, file operations, web requests) with the Hermes process owner's privileges.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes chat`
2. Ask the agent to execute any code that uses sandbox tools
3. In another terminal: `ls -la /tmp/hermes_rpc_*.sock`
4. Observe: socket has default permissions (world-accessible)

## Expected Behavior

The socket should be restricted to the owning user with `0o600` permissions.

## Actual Behavior

Socket is created with default permissions. Any local user can `ls /tmp/hermes_rpc_*.sock`, connect, and send JSON RPC requests to execute commands.

## Affected Component

- Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

## Root Cause Analysis

File: `tools/code_execution_tool.py`, line 944-945

```python
server_sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
server_sock.bind(sock_path)
server_sock.listen(1)
```

No `os.chmod(sock_path, 0o600)` after bind.

## Proposed Fix

Add `os.chmod(sock_path, 0o600)` after the bind call to restrict access to the owning user only.

## Bug Description
When using Hermes on Telegram, replying with a local image via the documented `MEDIA:/absolute/path/to/file.png` mechanism can result in Telegram receiving plain text containing the local filesystem path instead of a native uploaded photo attachment.

This was observed while trying to share a `browser_vision` screenshot.

## Expected Behavior
Per the Hermes docs and Telegram adapter implementation, a response containing `MEDIA:/absolute/path/to/file.png` should be intercepted by the gateway and delivered as a native Telegram photo upload.

## Actual Behavior
The user sees a plain text message like:

`🖼️ Image: /data/repo/home/cache/screenshots/browser_screenshot_2015cd1a9e244f10bc0e8a06269a34c4.png`

instead of receiving an attached image.

## Why this looks like a bug
I checked the public docs and upstream code:

- `website/docs/user-guide/features/browser.md` says browser screenshots shared on messaging platforms should be sent as native photo attachments via the `MEDIA:` mechanism.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py` extracts `MEDIA:<path>` tags.
- `gateway/platforms/telegram.py` implements `send_image_file(...)` to upload a local image as a Telegram photo.

So the intended behavior appears to be native attachment delivery, not path echoing.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use Hermes via Telegram DM.
2. Call `browser_vision` on any page so it returns a local `screenshot_path`.
3. Reply with exactly:
   `MEDIA:/absolute/path/to/the/screenshot.png`
4. Observe what Telegram receives.

## Observed Example
The screenshot path returned by `browser_vision` was:

`/data/repo/home/cache/screenshots/browser_screenshot_2015cd1a9e244f10bc0e8a06269a34c4.png`

The file existed on disk and was non-empty (~980 KB), but Telegram still showed the path as text instead of a photo attachment.

## Environment
- Platform: Telegram DM
- Hermes deployment: cloud-hosted/containerized deployment
- Screenshot source: `browser_vision`
- File path was absolute and existed on disk

## Notes / Suspicions
This may indicate one of the following:
- the `MEDIA:` tag is not being intercepted in this response path
- the platform send pipeline is falling back to the base adapter text behavior before Telegram native upload occurs
- some gateway/rendering path is converting the intended attachment send into plain text

I have not yet isolated whether this is a general Telegram issue or specific to certain deployment/gateway paths, but the behavior contradicts both the docs and the intended adapter flow.

items.body:
Since switching to MiniMax 2.7 highspeed, the gateway inactivity timeout (default 30 min) fires multiple times per day during active sessions. The agent appears to be waiting on an API response when no tool calls are being made, but sessions resume normally after /reset.

## Original error message

⏱️ Agent inactive for 30 min — no tool calls or API responses.
Last activity: API call #6 completed (4091s ago, iteration 6/100). The agent may have been waiting on an API response.
To increase the limit, set agent.gateway_timeout in config.yaml (value in seconds, 0 = no limit) and restart the gateway.
Try again, or use /reset to start fresh.

## Environment

- Model: MiniMax 2.7 highspeed
- Hermes version: 0.8.0
- OS: macOS (local), Arch Linux (Archie)

## Root Cause Analysis

The inactivity tracker (run_agent.py._touch_activity()) resets on every tool call, API call initiation, and stream token received. If 30 minutes pass with no activity, gateway/run.py (lines 7141–7210) triggers a timeout.

The mechanism was introduced in #4815 specifically to catch genuinely hung API calls — but it does not distinguish between a hung call and normal API latency during streaming responses.

It is unclear whether the repeated timeouts are caused by longer-than-expected MiniMax API response times, network latency, or something else. The pattern began after switching to MiniMax 2.7 highspeed and occurs multiple times per day.

## Related issues

- #4815 — original inactivity timeout implementation

An attacker could potentially send large or complex payloads that pass the size check but consume significant CPU during the fallback parsing. Implement strict Content-Type enforcement: only allow parsing if the Content-Type is explicitly 'application/json' or 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'.

items.title: Feature: Allow per-task model selection in delegate_task

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Feature Request: Per-task model selection in delegate_task

### Problem
Currently `delegate_task` does not expose a `model` parameter. Subagents always inherit the parent model or fall back to `delegation.model` from config. There is no way to select a different model per task at call time.

This is limiting for users who want tiered model routing — e.g. using a fast/cheap model (gemma4, 31B) for simple lookups and a powerful reasoning model (GLM-5.1, 128K context) for complex coding tasks.

### Proposed Solution
Add an optional `model` parameter to `delegate_task` at three levels:

1. **Per-task level** (in the `tasks` array items):
```json
{
  "goal": "simple lookup",
  "model": "gemma4:31b-cloud"
}
```

2. **Top-level `goal` call** (single task shorthand):
```json
{
  "goal": "check Champions League scores",
  "model": "gemma4:31b-cloud"
}
```

3. **Config default** (existing `delegation.model` in config.yaml):
Remains as the fallback when no per-task model is specified.

### Behavior
- `model` is **optional**. If omitted, falls back to `delegation.model` from config, or the parent agent model.
- The internal `_build_child_agent` function already supports `model`:
```python
effective_model = model or parent_agent.model
```
This just needs to be wired through from the public `delegate_task` API.
- The `DELEGATE_TASK_SCHEMA` also needs `model` added to the parameters.

### Suggested Implementation Hints
- Add `model: Optional[str] = None` to `delegate_task()` signature
- Add `model` to `DELEGATE_TASK_SCHEMA.properties`
- In the task loop, resolve `effective_model = task.get("model") or model or delegation_default`
- Pass `model=effective_model` through to `_build_child_agent()`

### Use Case Example
```python
# Fast cheap subagent for a lookup
delegate_task(goal="Check tonight's Champions League scores", model="gemma4:31b-cloud")

# Powerful reasoning subagent for complex refactor
delegate_task(goal="Refactor the auth module across 12 files", model="glm-5.1:cloud")

# Default model (from delegation.config or parent)
delegate_task(goal="Something moderate")
```

### Priority
Medium — enables better cost/performance tradeoffs for users with multi-model setups.

items.body:
## Bug Description

When Hermes is told to restart from Discord, the restart may begin or even succeed, but the original Discord message is often marked with a red `❌` and there is no reliable final confirmation message.

This makes an intentional self-restart look like a failure from the Discord UX, even when the restart itself likely worked.

This appears to be a remaining bug after #1414 / #1427:
- #1414 reported restart/shutdown weirdness more broadly
- #1427 fixed shutdown cleanup by canceling adapter background tasks and interrupting running agents during gateway shutdown
- current `main` still appears to treat intentional self-restart cancellation as ordinary processing failure for Discord reactions

## User-visible symptom

In Discord, a message such as `restart now` can get:
- an in-progress reaction
- then a final red `❌`
- and no trustworthy final "restart worked" acknowledgement

A follow-up message such as `did it work` may also get a red `❌` if the restart sequence is still interrupting the original processing lifecycle.

Observed screenshot behavior from local investigation:
- `restart now` receives a red `❌`
- the bot appears to emit restart-related terminal output
- a later `did it work` message also receives a red `❌`

## Concrete code path

Current `main` still has this cancellation-to-failure mapping in `gateway/platforms/base.py`:

- `gateway/platforms/base.py:1452-1454`
  - normal completion derives `processing_ok` and calls `on_processing_complete(..., processing_ok)`
- `gateway/platforms/base.py:1472-1474`
  - `asyncio.CancelledError` calls `on_processing_complete(..., False)` and re-raises

Current Discord reaction handling still maps `False` to a red `❌` in `gateway/platforms/discord.py`:

- `gateway/platforms/discord.py:741-748`
  - removes `👀`
  - adds `✅` if success else `❌`

That means an intentional self-restart can cancel the in-flight handler, trigger `on_processing_complete(..., False)`, and produce a false failure reaction in Discord.

## Why this is distinct from #1427

PR #1427 fixed an important shutdown bug:
- tracked adapter background tasks
- canceled them during shutdown
- interrupted running agents before disconnecting adapters

That addresses old gateway instances continuing to unwind work after shutdown/replacement.

But the remaining Discord UX problem appears narrower:
- intentional self-restart cancellation is still classified as ordinary failure for lifecycle completion
- Discord therefore shows `❌` for what may be a successful or expected restart transition

## Expected Behavior

On intentional self-restart from Discord:
- Hermes should not mark the triggering Discord message as failed purely because the handler was cancelled as part of restart/shutdown
- if a final confirmation message cannot be sent before restart, the bot should avoid a false red `❌`
- genuine handler errors should still surface as failure

## Acceptance Criteria

- intentional self-restart from Discord does not end with a false red `❌`
- cancellation caused by expected restart/shutdown is distinguished from genuine processing failure
- genuine errors still produce failure signaling
- regression coverage proves the Discord reaction lifecycle does not report false failure during self-restart

## Historical Context

- Related historical issue: #1414
- Related merged fix: #1427

## Bug: memory tool response leaks into Telegram output

### Description
When the `memory` tool is called (add/replace/remove), its internal response — including the old_text search string and operation indicators (+/-/~ prefixes) — is being rendered directly into the public Telegram message output.

Example of what appears in Telegram (user-visible):
```
🧠 memory: "+memory: "BUG: memory tool response...""
🧠 memory: "~memory: "Matrix homeserver UR""
🧠 memory: "-memory: "OpenClaw models via""
```

These are internal tool response artifacts that should never reach the user.

### Frequency
Seen multiple times by the same user.

### Environment
- Platform: Telegram
- Hermes gateway with user-mode systemd service

### Expected behavior
The memory tool should operate silently. Only the final confirmation (if any) should reach the user. The old_text string, operation markers (+/-/~), and internal state should never appear in the chat.

### Possible cause
The memory tool's response formatter may be passing raw operation metadata into the Telegram rendering layer instead of suppressing it for messaging platforms.

items.title: bug: check_for_updates reports stale 'commits behind' when ~/.hermes/hermes-agent exists as a separate repo

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Description

The `check_for_updates()` function in `hermes_cli/banner.py` checks for updates against `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` first (if `.git` exists there), falling back to the project root. When a user installs from source at a different path (e.g., `/Users/cortexuvula/hermes-agent`), the home-path repo becomes stale and `hermes --version` perpetually reports being N commits behind even when fully synced.

## Repro

1. Install hermes-agent at `/some/path/hermes-agent`
2. A copy or old install exists at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` (git repo, outdated)
3. Run `hermes update` — updates `/some/path/hermes-agent` successfully
4. Run `hermes --version` — still shows "N commits behind" because it checks `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`

## Root Cause

In `banner.py:133-148`:
```python
repo_dir = hermes_home / "hermes-agent"
if not (repo_dir / ".git").exists():
    repo_dir = Path(__file__).parent.parent.resolve()
```

It prefers `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` over the actual project root where the binary runs from.

## Fix

The update flow should either:
1. Also update `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` if it exists, or
2. `check_for_updates()` should prefer the project root (where `__file__` lives) over the home path, or  
3. The update command should delete or symlink the stale home-path repo

## Environment
- v0.8.0 (2026.4.8)
- macOS, installed at /Users/cortexuvula/hermes-agent
- Stale repo at ~/.hermes/hermes-agent (86 commits behind)

items.title: Bug: Session/Memory contamination between multiple agent instances

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

**Session Search and Memory are NOT isolated between multiple running instances/profiles of Hermes Agent.**

When multiple instances of Hermes Agent run simultaneously (e.g., different profiles like \"hermes-finance\", \"hermes\", etc.), their sessions and memories leak into each other. Specifically, `session_search` returns results from ALL instances, not just the current one.

---

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run 2+ instances of Hermes Agent with different configurations/profiles (e.g., one for finance/trading, one for general use)
2. Each instance operates in its own context with different cron jobs, reports, and session histories
3. From Instance A, run `session_search` or trigger any operation that queries long-term memory
4. Observe that results from Instance B (hermes-finance) leak into Instance A

---

## Evidence Found

**Multiple instances running simultaneously:**
```
PID 607635 — running since Apr04
PID 765830 — running since Abr05
PID 821347 — running since Abr06
```

**Directory structure showing isolated instance data:**
```
~/.hermes/
├── b3/                    # Finance/trading instance data (VALIDAÇÃO B3 reports)
│   ├── reports/           # validation_2026-04-06.json, validation_2026-04-07.json
├── cron/output/           # Empty — different instance owns this
└── channel_directory.json # Per-instance Telegram channels
```

**Config showing session grouping may be too broad:**
```yaml
session_reset:
  group_sessions_per_user: true  # This may be grouping ALL sessions together
```

---

## Expected Behavior

Each Hermes Agent instance/profile should have:
1. **Isolated session history** — `session_search` only returns results from the current instance
2. **Isolated memory** — Memory tool should not leak data between profiles
3. **Isolated cron job outputs** — Reports from Instance A should not appear in Instance B
4. **Clear profile/instance identification** — Each running instance should know its own identity

---

## Suggested Fixes

### 1. Add Instance/Profile ID to All Data Stores
Every session, memory entry, and cron output should be tagged with an instance identifier:
```python
session.metadata.instance_id = "hermes-finance"
memory.metadata.instance_id = "hermes-finance"
```

### 2. Filter session_search by Instance ID
```python
# In session_search implementation
results = query_sessions(query, filters={
    "instance_id": current_instance_id  # Only return sessions from THIS instance
})
```

### 3. Add Process-Level Isolation
Detect and warn when multiple instances are running:
- Show warning in logs when PIDs share same home directory
- Add `--instance-id` flag to distinguish profiles
- Consider using separate data directories per instance

### 4. session_reset.group_sessions_per_user Should Respect Instance Boundaries
Current behavior groups by user but ignores instance. Should group by `user + instance_id`.

### 5. Document Multi-Instance Architecture
If running multiple profiles is intentional, document:
- How to isolate data directories (`--data-dir`)
- How to name/identify instances
- Expected behavior of shared vs. isolated data

---

## Additional Context

- Hermes Agent version: 0.7.0
- Python 3.11
- Running on Linux (root/.hermes/)
- Multiple PIDs found via `ps aux | grep hermes-agent`

---

**Severity:** High — This is a data privacy/leakage issue between different agent personas/profiles.

items.title: add mempalace for external memory support
items.body:
Add a **mempalace** module to Hermes for structured external memory support. Repo here: https://github.com/milla-jovovich/mempalace
  This would give the agent persistent, queryable memory beyond the context
  window, enabling long-horizon tasks and cross-session continuity.

  ## Motivation

  Hermes currently operates within a single context window with no native
  mechanism for storing and retrieving knowledge across sessions or beyond
  context limits. A mempalace system would allow the agent to:

  - Persist learned facts, user preferences, and task context across sessions
  - Retrieve relevant memories via semantic search at inference time
  - Organize memories hierarchically (e.g., by topic, recency, importance)
  - Prune or consolidate stale memories automatically

  ## Proposed Design

  - **Storage backend**: Pluggable (local SQLite + vector embeddings by default,
   with support for external vector DBs)
  - **Ingestion**: Automatic extraction of key facts/decisions during
  conversations, plus explicit `remember` / `forget` commands
  - **Retrieval**: Semantic similarity search injected into the system prompt or
   tool results at query time
  - **Configuration**: New section in the Hermes config for memory settings (max
   entries, embedding model, storage path, TTL)
  - **Privacy**: All memory stored locally by default, with opt-in sync

  ## Open Questions

  - Should mempalace memories be scoped per-workspace, per-user, or global?
  - What embedding model should be used by default?
  - How should memory conflict resolution work when the same fact is updated
  across sessions?

items.title: Discord auto-thread names show raw role mention IDs
items.body:
## Bug

When auto-threading is enabled and a user mentions a role (e.g., `<@&1490963422786093149>`), the created thread name displays the raw mention syntax instead of stripping it.

**Expected behavior:** Thread names should show clean text without mention syntax.

**Actual behavior:** Thread names include literal `<@&...>` strings.

## Reproduction

1. Enable `DISCORD_AUTO_THREAD=true`
2. Mention a role in a server text channel
3. Observe the auto-created thread name includes the raw mention ID

## Root cause

In `_auto_create_thread()`, the thread name is built directly from `message.content` without stripping mention syntax. While user mentions (`<@...>`) are stripped from the message content before thread creation, role mentions (`<@&...>`) and channel mentions (`<#...>`) are not.

## Fix

Strip all Discord mention syntax from the content before constructing the thread name.
